intro.title: Explore Oceanarium Rosario Islands
intro.description:
Oceanarium Rosario Islands (Oceanario Islas del Rosario) is located in the Rosario Islands near Cartagena, Bolívar, Colombia. It is a world-class aquarium dedicated to marine biology research, conservation, and education.

As an important part of the Rosario and San Bernardo Corals National Natural Park, it showcases the rich Caribbean marine ecosystem, including coral reefs, tropical fish, sea turtles, and various marine species. The aquarium is not only a tourist attraction but also an important marine research and ecological conservation center.

visitGuide.title: Preparation & Tips
items: 🚢 Transportation: Take a speedboat from Cartagena pier, about 45-60 minutes to the Rosario Islands. It is recommended to book boat tickets in advance or join a day tour.
🧴 Sun Protection: The Caribbean region has strong sunlight. Please bring sunscreen, hat, and sunglasses to protect your skin from UV damage.
💧 Stay Hydrated: Tropical climate is hot and humid. Please bring enough drinking water to avoid heatstroke and dehydration.

alsoKnownAs.title: Marine Ecology & Conservation
items: 🐠 Coral Reef Ecosystem: The aquarium showcases healthy coral reef ecosystems around the Rosario Islands, one of the most important marine protected areas in Colombia's Caribbean region.
🐢 Sea Turtle Conservation: The aquarium participates in sea turtle protection and rehabilitation programs. Visitors can learn about the habits and conservation status of these marine reptiles.
🐬 Marine Mammals: Exhibits include marine mammals including dolphins, promoting marine ecological conservation knowledge.
♻️ Sustainable Tourism: Please follow the aquarium's rules, do not touch marine life, and help protect the fragile marine ecosystem.

officialManagement.title: About Oceanarium Rosario Islands
officialManagement.text: Oceanarium Rosario Islands is a famous marine biology research institution in Cartagena, Bolívar, Colombia, known for its Caribbean marine ecosystem exhibits and marine conservation research, supported by Colombia's National Natural Parks administration and relevant local governments.

historyTimeline.title: Historical Timeline

items.title: Early Period: Marine Conservation & Research
items.description: Oceanarium Rosario Islands, as an important part of the Rosario and San Bernardo Corals National Natural Park, has long been an important marine ecology research and conservation center in Colombia's Caribbean region.

items.title: 20th Century: Eco-Tourism Development
items.description: With the growth of tourism in Colombia, Oceanarium Rosario Islands gradually became one of the most popular marine eco-tourism destinations, attracting visitors from around the world.

items.title: 21st Century: Sustainable Development Recognition
items.description: As an important institution for marine conservation in Colombia's Caribbean region, the aquarium has gained international recognition and support, dedicated to marine ecological conservation and sustainable development education.

historyTimeline.guideContent: When visiting, you can take a speedboat from Cartagena to the Rosario Islands; then visit the aquarium's coral reef exhibits and marine life exhibition areas; if you have enough time, you can join snorkeling activities or explore the nearby beaches. Finally, return to Cartagena to explore this historic city.

route.title: Tour Guide
route.overview: There are mainly the following ways to explore Oceanarium Rosario Islands. Please choose according to your time and interests:
steps: Highlights: After taking a speedboat from Cartagena to the Rosario Islands, first visit the aquarium's main exhibition areas, including coral reef ecosystem, tropical fish gallery, sea turtle sanctuary, etc. You can enjoy lunch at the island's restaurant at noon.
In the afternoon, you can join snorkeling activities to explore the nearby coral reef ecosystem, or simply relax on the beach.
2. Day Tour Package (Suitable for tourists with limited time): About 6-8 hours

Highlights: If you have limited time or want a more convenient experience, you can choose a day tour package. The package usually includes round-trip transportation from Cartagena pier, aquarium tickets, lunch, and snorkeling gear rental.
supplements: Ticket prices vary by package. It is recommended to check and book online in advance, especially during peak tourist season.
Touching marine life is prohibited in the aquarium. Please follow the rules and protect the fragile marine ecosystem.
The Rosario Islands are located in the Caribbean Sea with strong sunlight. Please prepare for sun protection and bring enough water.

tickets.title: Oceanario Islas del Rosario Tickets & Prices
tickets.description: Oceanario Islas del Rosario ticket prices near Cartagena: adult and child rates, whether the boat from Cartagena is included, and where to buy tickets.
tickets.cardDesc: Adult and child rates, boat inclusion, and where to buy.
tickets.intro: The Oceanario Islas del Rosario (Oceanario CEINER) is a research aquarium on Isla San Martín de Pajarales. Here is how access and reference pricing work so you can plan your visit.

sections.heading: Reference pricing
sections.body: According to local tour operators, reference entry is about 40,000 COP for adults and 30,000 COP for children. Prices vary by operator and season; confirm at the official point of sale before your visit.

sections.heading: Does the price include the boat?
sections.body: Generally, the aquarium entry does NOT include the speedboat transfer from Cartagena. The boat is booked separately at the Cartagena docks (La Bodeguita or Muelle Turístico). Many day tours bundle both.

sections.heading: Where to buy
sections.body: You can buy entry at the Cartagena dock, through tour operators, or on online platforms. In high season (December–April) booking ahead is recommended.

sections.heading: Money-saving tips
sections.body: Day-tour packages usually include round-trip boat, aquarium entry, lunch, and snorkel gear, which is more convenient than booking each service separately.

faq.q: How much is the entry to the Oceanario?
faq.a: Reference pricing is around 40,000 COP (adults) and 30,000 COP (children) per local operators. These are not official aquarium prices and may change; verify at the point of sale before visiting.

faq.q: Does the price include the boat from Cartagena?
faq.a: Usually no. The boat fare is paid separately at the Cartagena docks. Organized tours typically include it in one package.

faq.q: Where do I buy tickets?
faq.a: At the Cartagena docks, via travel agencies, or online. Book ahead in high season to secure availability.

faq.q: Is there free entry for children?
faq.a: Some operators offer reduced or free entry for young children depending on the package. Check the current policy when buying.

getting-there.title: How to Get to Oceanario Islas del Rosario
getting-there.description: How to get to the Oceanario Islas del Rosario from Cartagena: speedboat from the dock, trip duration, airport options, and transport tips.
getting-there.cardDesc: Speedboat from Cartagena, trip duration, and airport options.
getting-there.intro: The Oceanario is on Isla San Martín de Pajarales in the Rosario Islands archipelago, about 45–60 minutes by boat from Cartagena.

sections.heading: Speedboat from Cartagena
sections.body: Take a fast boat from the Cartagena docks (La Bodeguita or Muelle Turístico) to the Rosario Islands. The trip takes about 45–60 minutes. Depart in the morning to make the opening hours.

sections.heading: From the airport
sections.body: From Rafael Núñez International Airport, first reach downtown Cartagena, then the dock to catch the boat.

sections.heading: Organized tours
sections.body: Many visitors choose a day tour that includes round-trip boat, entry, and lunch. It is the most convenient option if you don't want to arrange the boat yourself.

sections.heading: Transport tips
sections.body: Arrive at the dock 30 minutes before departure, bring sun protection and swimwear, and book your return in advance because boats usually leave the islands early.

faq.q: How do I get to the Oceanario from Cartagena?
faq.a: By fast boat from the Cartagena docks (La Bodeguita or Muelle Turístico); the trip is about 45–60 minutes.

faq.q: How long is the boat trip?
faq.a: Between 45 and 60 minutes, depending on sea conditions and the vessel.

faq.q: Is the Oceanario on Isla Grande?
faq.a: No. The Oceanario Islas del Rosario (CEINER) is on Isla San Martín de Pajarales in the Rosario Islands archipelago, not on Isla Grande.

faq.q: Can I go on my own or do I need a tour?
faq.a: You can go independently by hiring the boat at the dock, but a day tour is more convenient as it bundles transport, entry, and lunch.

tours.title: Oceanario Islas del Rosario Tours
tours.description: Tours to the Oceanario Islas del Rosario near Cartagena: full-day, snorkel, and private options, and what the packages include.
tours.cardDesc: Full-day, snorkel, and private tours, and what they include.
tours.intro: Tours are the easiest way to visit the Oceanario from Cartagena: they combine boat transport, entry, and activities in one package.

sections.heading: Full-day tour
sections.body: Includes round-trip boat, aquarium entry, lunch, and beach time. Ideal for short-stay visitors to Cartagena.

sections.heading: Snorkel tour
sections.body: Adds snorkel gear and time to explore nearby coral reefs. Recommended for sea lovers.

sections.heading: Private tour
sections.body: Private boat with flexible schedule, guide, and custom stops. Good for families or groups.

sections.heading: What packages include
sections.body: Varies by agency, but typically transport, entry, and lunch. Always confirm what is included before paying.

faq.q: What does a tour to the Oceanario include?
faq.a: Usually round-trip boat, aquarium entry, and lunch. Some add snorkel or visits to other islands.

faq.q: Is a guided tour worth it?
faq.a: Yes if you prefer convenience: the tour coordinates the boat, entry, and return, avoiding arranging each service yourself.

faq.q: Can it be combined with other islands?
faq.a: Yes, many tours combine the Oceanario with beaches or snorkeling on other Rosario islands.

faq.q: How much does a tour cost?
faq.a: Depends on the agency, season, and inclusions. Compare options in Cartagena and book ahead in high season.

hours.title: Oceanario Islas del Rosario Opening Hours
hours.description: Opening hours of the Oceanario Islas del Rosario near Cartagena, best time to visit, season, and how long the visit takes.
hours.cardDesc: Opening times, best time to visit, and how long to stay.
hours.intro: The Oceanario Islas del Rosario opens in the morning. Plan ahead because the boat transfer from Cartagena takes up much of the day.

sections.heading: Opening hours
sections.body: The aquarium is open from 09:00 to 13:30. We recommend confirming the schedule on the official site before your visit, as it may vary by season or weather.

sections.heading: Best time to go
sections.body: Arrive early in the morning. The sea is usually calmer and you'll have plenty of time before the boats depart.

sections.heading: Season
sections.body: High season is December–April (calm seas, good visibility). From May to November afternoon rain is possible.

sections.heading: Visit duration
sections.body: Allow at least 2–3 hours at the aquarium, plus the boat transfer (45–60 min each way).

faq.q: What are the Oceanario's hours?
faq.a: Open 09:00–13:30. Confirm on the official site before your visit.

faq.q: Which days is it open?
faq.a: Generally open every day in the morning; hours may shift for weather or season. Verify before leaving Cartagena.

faq.q: How long does the visit take?
faq.a: About 2–3 hours at the aquarium plus boat transport. Plan a full day if coming from Cartagena.

faq.q: Why is it only open in the morning?
faq.a: Because the return boat from the islands is usually scheduled at midday; the morning hours align with boat schedules.

cartagena-aquarium.title: Cartagena Aquarium Guide: Oceanario Islas del Rosario
cartagena-aquarium.description: Looking for the Cartagena aquarium? Learn where Oceanario CEINER is, how its island visit works, what to check before booking, and how to plan the boat trip.
cartagena-aquarium.cardDesc: Location, island access and a practical first-visit checklist.
cartagena-aquarium.intro: Searches for Cartagena aquarium, Acuario Cartagena and Oceanario Cartagena often refer to Oceanario Islas del Rosario (CEINER). It is not a walk-in aquarium in Cartagena's historic center: the marine conservation center is on Isla San Martín de Pajarales in the Rosario Islands.

sections.heading: Location and management
sections.body: The Oceanario is on Isla San Martín de Pajarales, within the Corales del Rosario y de San Bernardo national natural park area, offshore from Cartagena, Bolívar, Colombia. The Centro de Investigaciones, Educación y Recreación San Martín (CEINER) manages its research, education and conservation work.

sections.heading: How the visit fits into a day
sections.body: Begin at a Cartagena departure dock, take a prearranged boat to the islands, visit the marine exhibits and return on your booked service. Ask the operator to confirm a stop at San Martín de Pajarales: a generic Rosario Islands beach tour may not include the Oceanario. Allow extra time for boarding and changing sea conditions.

sections.heading: Tickets, pier fees and inclusions
sections.body: Before paying, request an itemized quote for the round-trip boat, Oceanario admission, any dock or park-related charges, lunch and optional activities. These can be sold separately. Check the applicable child policy and cancellation terms rather than assuming that all island tours offer the same package.

sections.heading: What to look for
sections.body: Use the visit to learn about Caribbean reef fish, marine habitats, turtles and coral restoration work. CEINER describes programs in marine research and conservation. The animals and activities available on a particular date can vary.

sections.heading: Before leaving Cartagena
sections.body: Verify the current visitor schedule, sailing time, return pier, sea conditions and whether the boat actually calls at the Oceanario. Carry sun protection, drinking water and protection for electronics. Follow staff instructions in the protected marine environment.

faq.q: Is the Cartagena aquarium in the city?
faq.a: No. Oceanario Islas del Rosario is on Isla San Martín de Pajarales, reached by boat from Cartagena.

faq.q: Is the Oceanario the same as Isla Grande?
faq.a: No. Isla Grande is a different island; make sure your boat stops at San Martín de Pajarales.

faq.q: Does every Rosario Islands tour include the aquarium?
faq.a: No. Ask for the Oceanario stop and admission to be listed explicitly in the booking.

faq.q: Where can I check the operator's information?
faq.a: See the Oceanario CEINER website at oceanario.co and confirm transport details with your boat provider.

marine-life.title: Marine Life & Conservation at Oceanario Rosario Islands
marine-life.description: Explore Oceanario CEINER's marine wildlife, coral restoration and educational conservation work, plus what to verify about dolphin experiences near Cartagena.
marine-life.cardDesc: Reef species, coral restoration and dolphin-activity questions.
marine-life.intro: The Oceanario combines a visitor experience with research and education about the Colombian Caribbean. This guide highlights what to observe and how to approach wildlife-related activities responsibly.

sections.heading: Caribbean reef fish and habitats
sections.body: Look for differences in body shape, swimming patterns and habitat between reef fish and open-water species. CEINER describes long-running marine fish research and aquaculture work; exhibits and interpretation may change.

sections.heading: Coral restoration
sections.body: Corals are living animals that build important reef habitat. CEINER documents coral-restoration work in the Rosario Islands. During the visit, ask how coral nurseries, monitoring and local stewardship contribute to reef recovery.

sections.heading: Sharks, rays and sea turtles
sections.body: The center's conservation work also involves elasmobranchs such as sharks and rays. Ask guides which species are currently present and how animal welfare and research are managed. Do not assume every animal mentioned in online descriptions will be visible on the day.

sections.heading: Dolphins near Cartagena: check first
sections.body: If you are looking for dolphin-related activities, distinguish watching an educational presentation from any separately sold close-contact experience. Availability, rules, age restrictions and pricing can change; ask the Oceanario directly before booking. Do not assume swimming is included with standard admission.

sections.heading: Photography and responsible visiting
sections.body: Photograph from permitted viewing areas, avoid flash where prohibited, never feed or touch animals without explicit staff guidance, and keep all litter out of the sea. Use interpretation signs and staff explanations to understand the animals rather than relying on staged-photo expectations.

faq.q: Can I see dolphins at the Oceanario?
faq.a: Dolphins are mentioned in visitor information, but specific presentations and close-contact activities are not guaranteed. Confirm the current program with CEINER.

faq.q: Is swimming with dolphins included?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Ask the Oceanario directly about whether an activity is offered, its rules and its separate price.

faq.q: Does CEINER work on coral conservation?
faq.a: Yes. Its published research pages describe coral restoration and other marine conservation projects.

faq.q: What should families focus on?
faq.a: Marine habitats, reef fish, coral conservation and questions for guides about the Colombian Caribbean ecosystem.
